introduction.text: The Casa di Diana, also known as the Caseggiato di Diana, is an ancient Roman insula located in Regio I of Ostia. It is significant for its well‑preserved residential architecture, terracotta relief of the goddess Diana, and evidence of early Roman urban life.

history.description: The insula was built in the first half of the 2nd century AD, likely on the site of an earlier domus.
A small mitre was discovered during excavations in 1914–1915.
The site was first investigated by Guido Calza between 1914 and 1916.
Further excavations were carried out by Alfredo Marinucci from 1994 to 1997.
The insula was constructed over an older Roman domus.

design.description: The building is organized around a porticoed courtyard, with multiple floors—possibly five—housing residential units and ground‑floor taverns.
Arcades surround the courtyard; later they were filled in, and a covered cistern was built above a terracotta relief of Diana.
The north façade of the first floor featured niches intended for small sculptures.

art.description: A terracotta relief depicting the goddess Diana holding a bow and arrow, a dog, and a deer, located above the cistern.
Several rooms on the upper floors contain frescoed walls, and some taverns have remnants of frescoes.
A polychrome mosaic on the ground‑floor courtyard and a marble basin with mosaic floors were found.
